chunks.heading: Who I am
chunks.text: Who I am. I am Zaid Haris, a second-year BEng Robotics, Mechatronics and Control Engineering student at Loughborough University. I am interested in robotics, mechatronics and AI.

chunks.heading: Where I am based
chunks.text: Where I am based. I am based in Leicester, UK, and I study at Loughborough University.

chunks.heading: Education
chunks.text:
Education. I started at Loughborough in 2025. My Year 1 modules included Applied Engineering, Core Maths, Dynamic Systems Analysis, and Programming and Software Engineering. My Year 2 modules include Control System Design, Robotic Systems Technology, and Project Design and Management.

Before that I did my A-Levels at Beauchamp College (Maths A, Computer Science C, Physics C) and my GCSEs at Manor High School (nine, including Maths 9 and English 7).

chunks.text: Outside work. I play padel, enjoy strategy games such as chess and Clash Royale, build model kits, and read comics and books.

chunks.text: Freelance Web Developer (self-employed). I designed, built and hosted live websites that have had over 15,000 visitors in total, including The Great British Curry Festival.

chunks.text: Technical Coordinator at Ada Innovate (Oct 2023 to June 2024, Cardiff, contract). I ran the technology side of an international academic conference, from planning through to AV and technical support on the day.

chunks.text: Virtual Work Experience with Ford, GE Aerospace and JLR (Oct to Nov 2024). At Ford I worked on battery testing and ROS package integration. At GE Aerospace I looked at propulsion energy sources. For JLR I did the Drive Your Future programme.

chunks.text: Volunteer at the Smallpeice Trust STEM Day (Mar 2024). I helped students assemble and test model planes, working through problems with them as they came up.

chunks.heading: Autonomous EV Charging Robot (group coursework, simulation)
chunks.text: Autonomous EV Charging Robot (group coursework, simulation). I led design engineering and project management for a team of 6 on a simulated EV charging robot with an arm, LiDAR and computer vision. We identified 9 failure modes, with a mitigation for each. I chose the actuators and motors and worked with my teammates to fit them into the team's CAD.

chunks.heading: Adaptive Low-Power Temperature Monitor (Arduino, individual coursework)
chunks.text: Adaptive Low-Power Temperature Monitor (Arduino, individual coursework). I built an Arduino data logger that adjusts its sampling rate using an on-board DFT and the Nyquist criterion. I cut the sampling rate by 50% (from 1 Hz to about 0.5 Hz) on a slow signal, within an estimated 1.5 KB of the board's 2 KB of SRAM. I logged the data over serial and analysed it in Python. The code is on GitHub.

chunks.heading: Autonomous Digital Flight Simulator (personal project)
chunks.text: Autonomous Digital Flight Simulator (personal project). A flight simulator in Python, using object-oriented code and custom control loops for navigation and flight paths.

chunks.heading: Week 1 project: Ground Truth (AI evaluation)
chunks.text: Week 1 project: Ground Truth (AI evaluation). I hand-labelled 30 news headlines into four categories (World, Sports, Business and Sci/Tech), had an AI model label the same 30 with two different prompts, and compared everything against the official AG News labels. My labels agreed with the official ones 80% of the time (Cohen's kappa 0.73). Business and Sci/Tech were confused most. I also showed that always answering World scores 80% accuracy on an imbalanced set but a kappa of 0.00, and that a TF-IDF classifier tested on its own training data scored 1.00 against 0.62 when tested honestly.

chunks.heading: Week 2 project: Newsroom Triage (deployed app)
chunks.text: Week 2 project: Newsroom Triage (deployed app). I put a Python news classifier on GitHub with automated tests that run on every change, fixed its three failing tests, deployed it on Render, and added a feature that asks the model twice when it is unsure. Its accuracy on my 30 test headlines went from 20% to about 83% to 87% (25 or 26 of 30) once I found that the model's replies were being cut off by a token limit. The free hosting took 65 seconds to wake up after sitting idle.

chunks.heading: Week 3 project: this portfolio chat
chunks.text: Week 3 project: this portfolio chat. This page has a chat that answers questions about me from my own notes. It is deployed on Vercel, and I am measuring how well its retrieval works.

chunks.text: Robotics and control. Control loop design, ROS package integration, and project coordination. I led a team of 6 on a simulated robot project.

chunks.text: Tools and practice. Git and GitHub, GitHub Actions, technical documentation, iterative testing and debugging, and risk assessment. I have deployed apps on Render and Vercel and used Google Colab and the Groq API.
